Subject: Next steps: Key custody and SOC 2 alignment for MedPulse POC

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and a few action items so we don’t lose momentum. Short version: MedPulse wants to validate that Redwood can meet SOC 2 + HIPAA constraints for the POC and prefers to discuss customer-managed keys for high-sensitivity PHI workloads.

Call recap (high level)
- Scope: prototype serving of anonymized clinical notes + embeddings for search/retrieval.
- Compliance baseline: MedPulse expects SOC 2 Type II evidence, HIPAA-compliant handling, and data residency in us-east1.
- Key ask: ability for MedPulse to control encryption keys (BYOK/CMK) or to have dedicated HSM-backed key custody.

Open items / questions for your security team:
1) Do you require full BYOK (customer uploads key material to their KMS/HSM) or would a Redwood-hosted CMK with customer-managed rotation meet your controls?
2) Expected key usage patterns: will you want per-tenant CMKs, or a single project-level key for the POC?
3) Audit expectations: specific log retention windows, evidence format for SOC 2 (e.g., key access logs, HSM access logs).

Next steps (proposed)
- I’ll kick off a short security questionnaire to capture the technical asks (see attached template). Please fill the sheet and return by EOD Thu so we can loop in Product Security.
- Internally I’ll put Laura + Karthik on the thread for the technical design and Marissa for ops considerations.

Attachments: medpulse_kms_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet) — lightweight template to capture KMS/HSM, rotation, backup, and audit requirements.

If that plan works, I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review the filled sheet and a proposed key custody model.

Thanks —

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side before you loop in engineering/security: 

1) BYOK vs CMK: For the POC we are willing to accept a Redwood-hosted CMK only if we get proof of HSM-backend and proof that Redwood cannot export key material. For production, we expect customer control (BYOK with our KMS).

2) Per-tenant keys: Prefer per-tenant keys for separation. During POC a per-project key is ok as long as the audit trail maps requests to tenant IDs.

3) Audit & evidence: SOC 2 is table stakes — we’ll need sample audit logs showing key usage (timestamps, requester id, operation). Retention 2 years for logs for higher-risk flows.

4) HIPAA: we need confirmation that egress encryption in transit uses TLS1.2+ with mutual auth for private deployments; and at-rest encryption must be AES-256.

I’ve attached a baseline list (security@medpulse.health) — I’ll have our security lead Tom jump into the thread once you fill out the template.

Asha Rao
Head of Product Security, MedPulse Health

Quick readout from Security/Product: short answers and suggested customer-facing language.

Feasibility: YES (short-term POC path)
- Redwood can offer a HSM-backed CMK with non-exportable key material. We currently support HSM-backed CMKs via our KMS integrations (AWS CloudHSM / Google Cloud HSM).
- Evidence we can provide quickly: key-usage logs (sample CSV extract), KMS audit trail (console export), and a vendor attestation letter (if required). We can package these as SOC 2-relevant artifacts for the POC.

Per-tenant vs per-project keys:
- For the POC we recommend per-project CMK with tenant-level request tagging (maps to MedPulse tenant IDs). Per-tenant CMKs are supported but add on-boarding overhead (each key provisioning and rotate cycle). If the customer needs strict crypto separation for the POC, we can scope per-tenant keys but expect ~2–3 extra business days to provision and validate.

BYOK path (production):
- Production BYOK (customer-managed key material) is supported (customer uploads public-wrapped key material or uses a cloud KMS integration). This requires additional compliance paperwork and onboarding flows (KMS access, shared rotation schedule).

Audit retention and logs:
- We can provide key-usage logs with 2-year retention as a paid retention add-on. For the POC we can export a 90-day sample and negotiate retention in the contract.

TLS/HIPAA:
- Transport: TLS1.2+ enforced. For private deployments we support mutual TLS.
- At-rest: AES-256. HSM-backed CMKs use approved key sizes and non-exportable flags.

Next recommended message to customer (suggested to Priyom):
1) Offer the HSM-backed Redwood CMK for POC, include a sample key-usage CSV and vendor attestation in the follow-up.
2) Ask whether they want per-tenant keys for the POC; if yes, state the ~2–3 business day provisioning overhead.
3) Confirm willingness to accept short-term 90-day log samples while negotiating 2-year retention as part of the contract.

I’ll attach a sample CSV extract and the attestation for the follow-up email. Laura — can you confirm cost delta for 2-year retention so Priyom can share with procurement? Marissa — any ops caveats for per-tenant key provisioning?

— Karthik
